title: Supporting decision-making capacity in oncology. Development and piloting of a multimodal intervention
summary:
People with cancer face difficult decisions over the course of their treatment.
To make these decisions well, they need information from the different health professionals. They also have at least one lengthy conversation with the doctor treating them about the options for treatment. This conversation is called a pre-treatment consultation. The aim of this information and the conversation is to prepare the patient to make an informed decision. This means that patients know the advantages and disadvantages of the different treatment options and can decide according to their own wishes and goals. Informed consent to treatment is usually documented in writing.
However, some of the information materials and consent form used so far are difficult to understand, for example because they contain a lot of technical terms or statistics or are very detailed. We would like to improve this situation. 

Together with a team from the fields of ethics, medicine, law and sociology, we are trying to create better consent forms and information materials that are easier for patients to understand. These are also offered in digital formats (e.g. videos, etc.). We involve people who have already had cancer in the development of these materials and therefore know what information would have been helpful for them. In addition, doctors and nurses are interviewed to find out what is important to them. In a final step, the existing scientific literature is reviewed for relevant information.

Even though these information materials would be important for all people with cancer, the study focuses on three groups of people: 1) people with lung cancer, 2) people with oesophageal cancer, 3) people with liver cancer.

The new documents are not only being developed, but we also want to check whether they are better than the current documents.. For this purpose, we are conducting a so-called before-and-after study. 130 hospital patients will be asked about several points before the new documents are used: 1) How capable are you or how ready do you feel to make a decision? 2) How anxious do you feel? 3) How satisfied were you with the documents and the conversation?
We take time afterwards to make sure that the hospital staff also use our new documents. Afterwards, other patients will be asked the same questions. We hope that the questions will be answered better after using our information materials than before. We will present our results at a final conference in winter 2025.
conditions: Squamous cell carcinoma of the oesophagus stage IV; (non-) small cell lung carcinoma stage IV; hepatocellular carcinoma stage C

interventions.name:
The intervention is in the development phase and will be completed in December 2023.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. indication of a systemic therapy
2. understanding of the German language
Exclusion criteria:
1. lack of or unclear capacity to give consent or presence of a legal guardian
2. lack of ability to speak, e.g. due to severe mucositis
3. patient is in the dying phase
